label: GO: choosing a1 after a rewarded streak, first ~70 trials of the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never D1/D2). Needs the last outcome to be rewarded (prev_reward==1; zero activation after an unrewarded trial) and the agent to be choosing a1 (97% of mass is on model_act==a1; activation is strongest when the a1 logit margin is very large, top choice bin 72% of mass). It is mostly silent on the first rewarded trial after a loss: requiring the trial before that to be rewarded too (or outside the window) lifts precision from 0.63 to 0.80. It also depends on time in the episode: active in trials 10-69, falling off in 70-79 and completely silent from trial 80 on. The value head tracks this (value falls over the episode), so value > 7.3 works almost as well as ep_trial < 70 (dev F1 0.82 vs 0.83). Magnitude grows over a rewarded a1 streak, e.g. 0.2 -> 0.46 -> 0.60 -> 1.0 over consecutive trials. Remaining misses are weak activations on rewarded a2 choices (3% of mass). Uses only observed variables plus the current choice of the agent.

issues: Missing state condition. The unit needs the last reward to have come from S1, not just any reward. With phase==GO & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==2 & model_act==1, precision is exactly 0.000 (6594 dev steps). Inside the original predicate, the subset with prev_state==2 (mostly a1 -> S2 rare, rewarded, then a1 again) has dev P 0.000 on 4272 steps and test P 0.000 on 3855 steps. That is the predicate's largest systematic false-positive class, so the claim 'the last outcome must be rewarded' is too broad.

Breaking it down by transition shows the same thing. With the original predicate plus prev_common==0, P is 0.104; plus prev_common==1, P is 0.934. Plus prev_action==2 (a2 -> S1 rare, rewarded), P is 0.817, so what matters is the state reached, not the transition or the previous action.

The tv('prev_reward',-1)!=0 condition is trivially true at rel -3, where the lookup falls outside the window and returns -9. Predicate precision at rel -3 is only 0.67, versus about 0.90 at rel -2..0. So the 'trial before must also be rewarded' condition only does work inside the window.

A loss two trials back does not silence the unit equally. When it was an unrewarded visit to S2, P is 0.033; when it was an unrewarded visit to S1, P is 0.316. The 'trial before must be rewarded' rule is a simplification.

Claims that check out: GO-only (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps); prev_reward==0 gives 0 activation; 97% of mass is on model_act==a1; the top choice-logit bin holds 72% of mass; ep_trial 80+ is completely silent and 70-79 is weak; the value>7.3 substitute gives dev F1 0.819. Reported scores reproduce: test P 0.795, R 0.85, F1 0.822, mass recall 0.938. The predicate uses no future variables.

The label's 'rewarded streak' overclaims. The predicate only requires the last two outcomes to be rewarded, or one at the window edge. Requiring three (adding tv('prev_reward',-2)!=0) lowers dev F1 to 0.783.

The remaining misses are weak activations on a2 choices after a reward at S1: prev_reward==1 & prev_state==1 & model_act==2 gives P 0.286 and about 6% recall, matching the roughly 3% of mass the explanation reports.
